title: U.S. House · Florida's 2nd District
area: The eastern Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend region, including Panama City to Tallahassee.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Neal Dunn did not make the ballot in the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, which Austin Rogers won with 30.3% in an eight-candidate field. Amanda Green won the Democratic primary with 33.4% over three opponents.

candidates.name: Amanda Green
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 33.4% over three opponents.

summary.text: Amanda Green is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 2nd Congressional District seat. A Florida State University graduate, she describes a career in operations and pricing roles supporting global health programs, beginning with a USAID partner organization. She is running on an affordability, anti-corruption and government-accountability platform.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree (2015) and a graduate degree (2017) from Florida State University, according to Ballotpedia; she says she studied international development, economics and public administration.
Began her career with what she calls a leading USAID partner organization.
Says she worked for about a decade as an operations director and pricing expert supporting global health programs, famine monitoring systems, and relief efforts in Ukraine.
According to WFSU, her campaign website says she worked for a subsidiary of USAID until the agency was cut back after President Trump returned to office.
Entered the race after Rep. Neal Dunn announced his retirement; Ballotpedia lists no earlier campaigns or offices for her.
Won the August 18, 2026 four-way Democratic primary over Yen Bailey, Nicholas Zateslo and Brice Barnes; WFSU reports endorsements from the AFL-CIO and Leon County Sheriff Walt McNeil.
Campaign priorities she lists include lowering housing and gas costs, banning congressional stock trading, enacting term limits, and holding regular in-person town halls across the district.

priorities.text: Addressing the affordability crisis by supporting farmers, lowering housing costs, banning corporate ownership of single-family homes, and protecting Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and veterans' benefits.
Restoring accountability in government by banning congressional stock trading and enacting term limits.
Holding regular in-person and virtual town halls with constituents.

positions.summary: Says she will protect Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and veterans' benefits as part of addressing the affordability crisis.

statements.quote: We will see a reduction in costs when we see the overhead the the middlemen removed from our health insurance.
statements.context: At the Aug. 2026 Capital Tiger Bay Club forum, per WFSU

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, WFSU forum coverage and WCTV debate coverage reviewed. No campaign-website issue pages fetched; her survey answers on abortion are blank per Ballotpedia. No position found on other tracked issues.

candidates.name: Austin Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 30.3% in an eight-candidate field; incumbent Neal Dunn withdrew before the primary and is listed by Ballotpedia as a withdrawn candidate.

summary.text: Austin Rogers, a Panama City attorney and former General Counsel to U.S. Sen. Rick Scott, is the Republican nominee for the open Florida 2nd Congressional District seat. He grew up in Bay County, earned a law degree from Duke University, and is running for his first elected office. According to his campaign website, he is running to support President Trump's agenda; he has also named jobs, affordability and artificial intelligence as priorities.

background.text: Born and raised in Bay County and a lifelong Panama City native, according to his campaign website; he graduated from Mosley High School and played college soccer.
Earned his law degree from Duke University.
Worked briefly in Washington, D.C., then moved back to the district with his wife, according to Fox News.
Served as General Counsel to Sen. Rick Scott's Senate office, where he says he drafted legislation, conducted congressional hearings and led investigations.
According to his campaign website, his father flew two tours with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds and retired from Tyndall Air Force Base, and his mother worked as a local schoolteacher.
Launched his campaign for the seat Rep. Neal Dunn is leaving; Ballotpedia lists no earlier campaigns or offices for him.

Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 30.47% of the vote in a field that included Keith Gross, Evan Power and Luke Murphy; he has said he would prioritize the Safe Kids Act, which he says continues a bill he worked on with Sen. Scott.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Hala, a dermatologist, live in Panama City with their three children.

priorities.text: Says he will be a reliable vote for President Trump's agenda in Congress.
Lists securing the border, backing law enforcement and the military, and defending what he calls Florida values as priorities.
Says he will defend the Constitution and use his legal and legislative experience to stop what he considers bad bills.

positions.summary: Describes himself as opposed to abortion from conception and says he will support policies protecting the unborn.
positions.quote: Austin believes that life is sacred and is 100% pro life from conception.

positions.summary: Opposes new gun-control measures and says he will defend the 2nd Amendment and the rights of gun owners.
positions.quote: Austin will stand firmly against any radical gun control agenda pursued by the Radical Left and work to protect the rights of law-abiding gun owners.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he opposes transgender athletes' participation in women's sports, using the wording quoted.
positions.quote: Austin believes that biological men have no business participating in women’s sports.

candidates.researchNotes: No completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found; positions and biography drawn from his campaign website.
